input.quote: 12.4 During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.
input.rationale: § 12.4 binds the Customer (us) with a post-term non-compete of twenty-four months covering any competing product or service in any territory, with no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions (indeed acquisitions are expressly captured). That is walk-away territory under the rule: post-term duration exceeds 12 months and the scope is undefined/unlimited, so it fails the fallback (single named product, term only, ≤12 months, with carve-outs). It also directly contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no exclusivity or non-compete commitment. We propose deleting § 12.4 to reach the preferred position, and can offer the narrowed fallback if the Vendor shows a genuine need.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the products or services we develop, buy or sell, so we have deleted the non-compete in § 12.4; it also directly contradicts § 12.3, which confirms we have made no non-compete commitment. If some protection is genuinely needed, we could consider a narrow restriction on a single named competing product, during the term only, with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.
proposal.summary: Delete the 24-month, all-product, all-territory non-compete binding Customer.
